title: Swiggy Shares Plunge 17% to 52-Week Low as Instamart Losses Widen
excerpt: Swiggy fell to Rs 174.90 after Q2 FY27 results showed Instamart's adjusted EBITDA loss widening to Rs 895 crore, prompting target cuts from Citi, CLSA, Nomura, HSBC and others even as most kept their ratings.
body:
• Swiggy shares plunged as much as 17.23% on Friday to a 52-week low of Rs 174.90 on the BSE, a day after the company's Q2 FY27 results.
  • Swiggy's consolidated net loss was Rs 922 crore — narrower than a year earlier but wider than the June quarter — as revenue rose 36% year on year to Rs 7,571 crore.
  • Instamart's adjusted EBITDA loss widened to Rs 895 crore, and at least eight brokerages cut their price targets, though most kept their ratings.
  • What it means for investors: the stock closed the morning near Rs 181, down about 14% from Thursday's close of Rs 211.30, and brokerage targets now span Rs 230 (Macquarie) to Rs 375 (UBS) — the disagreement is almost entirely about how fast Instamart stops losing money.

Swiggy's shares plunged as much as 17.23% to a 52-week low of Rs 174.90 on the BSE on Friday, according to Inc42, a day after the food delivery and quick commerce company reported September-quarter results that showed its Instamart arm losing more money even as its core food business improved. The stock later pared some losses to trade at Rs 181.50, down 14.10%, with a market capitalisation of about Rs 50,100 crore.

The quarter behind the sell-off

Swiggy's consolidated net loss narrowed about 16% year on year to Rs 922 crore in Q2 FY27, but widened 17% from Rs 791 crore in the preceding quarter, Inc42 reported. Operating revenue rose 36% year on year to Rs 7,571 crore. The split inside the company was stark. Food delivery operating revenue rose 22% year on year to Rs 2,338 crore and segment profit increased 39% to Rs 349 crore. Instamart moved the other way: its adjusted EBITDA loss increased to Rs 895 crore, from Rs 849 crore a year earlier and Rs 778 crore in Q1 FY27, and its segment loss widened to Rs 764 crore.

Instamart's gross order value grew 31% year on year to Rs 9,230 crore, IANS reported, and net order value growth accelerated to 13.4% quarter on quarter. But its contribution margin deteriorated to minus 1.4% from minus 0.3% in Q1, as growth was driven by customer incentives and higher fixed costs. The platform added 69 dark stores in the quarter, taking its network to 1,240 stores across 133 cities, and monthly transacting users rose by 1.3 million to 14.8 million.

"Our food delivery business delivered its highest ever profits and margins while we continue to unlock new category growth through Toing, our standalone offering for affordable meals."

— Sriharsha Majety, Cofounder, MD and Group CEO, Swiggy

Brokerages cut targets, keep ratings

The analyst response was a near-uniform round of target cuts without rating downgrades. Citi kept its Buy rating but cut its target to Rs 330, noting food delivery gross order value growth of 18% year on year while Instamart's net order value growth of about 13% sequentially missed its 16% estimate. Jefferies also kept a Buy rating and a Rs 330 target, saying reducing quick commerce losses remains critical. Nomura kept a Buy rating with a Rs 300 target, valuing food delivery at 40 times estimated FY28 EBITDA and assigning no value to quick commerce. CLSA retained Outperform but lowered its target to Rs 262, flagging a widening gap with Eternal, the parent of Zomato and Blinkit, in growth and profitability.

The cautious end of the street was blunter. HSBC kept a Hold rating but cut its target to Rs 240 from Rs 315, citing food delivery market share losses and intensifying competition. Bank of America cut its target to Rs 245 from Rs 275 and flagged possible cannibalisation of Swiggy's main food business by Toing, its affordable-meals offering. Macquarie maintained Underperform at Rs 230. UBS was the outlier, holding Buy at Rs 375 despite calling the results weaker than expected.

What Swiggy says happens next

Management told analysts it believes Instamart's adjusted EBITDA losses peaked in Q2 FY27. The company expects double-digit sequential net order value growth in Q3 FY27 and an improvement of about 100 basis points in adjusted EBITDA margin. Swiggy also plans to begin shifting Instamart to an inventory-led model by mid-Q3 FY27, a transition expected to take two to three quarters. The company expects the shift to improve Instamart's contribution margin by about 80 basis points and shorten its working capital cycle by eight to 10 days.

That guidance is now the test for the stock. Friday's fall prices in deep scepticism that quick commerce economics will turn on schedule while Blinkit sets the pace. If Instamart's losses narrow in the December quarter as promised, the Buy ratings at nearly double the current price will look early rather than wrong; if they widen again, Friday's low is unlikely to be the last.
